Both films are made by Geoshield. VLT = visible light let through (lower is darker). TSER = total solar energy rejected. IR = infrared heat rejected. Figures from the manufacturer spec sheets.

Carbon vs. Ceramic: what's the difference?

Carbon film uses carbon particles to block heat and UV. It's affordable, keeps the cabin cooler, and doesn't affect signals. Ceramic film uses non-metallic, non-conductive ceramic particles and gives the strongest heat rejection and UV protection we offer. Pick ceramic for peak performance and carbon for the best balance of performance and price. Not sure? Ask for a quote on both.

California Tint Law

Know the limits

Top 4"
WindshieldNon-reflective tint is allowed on the top 4 inches.
70%+
Front side windowsMust let in more than 70% of light.
Any
Rear side windowsNo specific darkness limit. If the rear window is tinted, dual side mirrors are required.
✕
Restricted colorsRed, amber, and yellow tints are not permitted.
Rx
Medical exemptionsAllowed with a certificate from a dermatologist, ophthalmologist, or optometrist.

Tint laws change. Check with local law enforcement or the California DMV for the latest rules, and look for any county or city ordinances.

FAQ

Common questions

What's the difference between carbon and ceramic?

Carbon film blocks heat and UV with carbon particles. It's cost-effective and won't interfere with signals. Ceramic film uses non-metallic ceramic particles for the best heat rejection, UV protection, and thermal insulation. Choose ceramic for peak performance and carbon for a balance of performance and price.

How do I get a quote or appointment?

Fill out the quote form with your vehicle details. We'll get back to you quickly with pricing for ProNano Ceramic, C2 Carbon, or both. Then let us know what time works and we'll match schedules.

What's the legal tint limit in California?

Non-reflective tint on the top 4 inches of the windshield, more than 70% light on the front side windows, and no specific limit on rear side windows. If the rear window is tinted, dual side mirrors are required. Red, amber, and yellow tints aren't allowed. See the tint law section for details.

What should I expect after my windows are tinted?

More privacy, better UV protection, less glare day and night, and a sleeker look. Important: don't roll down any freshly tinted windows for a few days so the film can fully set.

Do you remove old tint?

Yes. If your current film is peeling, bubbling, faded, hazy, or discolored, select tint removal on the quote form and tell us which windows need it.
